- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is flat or rising slowly, adjust upward by 2–5% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior period), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 5–7 days to avoid overshoot.
- If supply net is negative and bullish events dominate, model often underestimates upside; add 3–8% buffer to forecast mean if bullish sentiment >0.67.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤-0.5) and model is still rising, force downward correction by 3–7% to align with sentiment drift.
- For 30-day forecasts, if recent 18-day history shows volatility >10% or sentiment swings >0.5, apply mean reversion bias: forecast = 0.8×prior + 0.2×current trend.
- When official events show high bearish balance (net < -15) and sentiment is neutral or bearish, model often overestimates recovery; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 7 days.
- If model forecast is rising steadily but true outcome shows early dip or reversal, assume sentiment shift; reduce forecast slope by 15–25% for next 3–5 days.
